staleness_test.definition: judge row scored_at < reader row scored_at for the same question_id => stale by construction

second_independent_test.signature: attempts == 0 AND llm_judge_raw == '' AND resolved_snapshot is null
second_independent_test.meaning: the judge API was never called for these rows; absence of a verdict was recorded as false

staleness_test.concentration_conclusion: The two question types reading 0.0 (knowledge-update, single-session-assistant) are exactly the two types that are 100% stale. temporal-reasoning is 45.1% stale and reads 0.543. Every type with zero stale rows scores identically to judge_gpt4o_v2. The low score is fully explained by the stale set.

positive_control_on_the_judge.conclusion: The judge itself never disagreed. judge_gpt4o is the same judge run against an incomplete input, not a different judge result.

findings.code: response = row.get("response") or ""; if not response: verdict, raw, attempts, resolved_snapshot = False, "", 0, None
findings.effect: An empty reader response short-circuits to a false verdict with NO judge call. This is the exact 194-row signature.

findings.code: done_ids built from question_id presence in rescored.jsonl; rows in done_ids are skipped
findings.effect: Resume keys on EXISTENCE, not freshness. Re-running into the same out-dir skips every row already present, however it was scored. Root cause.

findings.code: rescore_summary.json and control_receipt.json recomputed and overwritten on every invocation; resolved_snapshots filters falsy values
findings.effect: A resume invocation that judges zero rows still rewrites the summary and control receipt, and the summary structurally cannot show the 194 null snapshots.

recommendations.detail: Add SUPERSEDED.md / NOTE.md in-directory: partial artifact, 194/500 rows never judged (attempts 0, empty raw, null snapshot), judged against a checkpoint reader.log had already declared ARTIFACT INVALID, yields 289/500, authoritative pass-1 verdicts are in judge_gpt4o_v2/, and the shipped control receipt is from a later resume invocation that judged no rows.
One clause naming full-v34-opus_pass1/judge_gpt4o/ as superseded. Silence is what makes the naming convention hazardous — the unsuffixed name reads as canonical.
The paper already documents the identical one-row defect on the xhigh pass. Give the 194-row headline-pass instance the same sentence; it strengthens the fail-closed-audit story.

(a) refuse to resume into an out-dir whose rescored.jsonl contains any row with attempts == 0 (non-verdicts are not completed work); (b) refuse to judge a reader checkpoint whose run_meta audit is not clean, unless forced. Root cause is resume keying on existence rather than freshness.
Optional: emit a per-judge-dir integrity column (rows, attempts==0 count) so the manifest would have exposed this. Today it proves only that bytes did not drift.
